seed: Verified note: kffm (Shannon). Byron, 16-Nov-2026: KFFM deep dive.

slides.title: Is your KFFM still right?
slides.headline: Is your KFFM still right?
notes: If the KFFM is not in Metronome yet, show the Kick Off picture.
Ask each owner: what do you need to do to turn it green?
slides.support: Put your current KFFM on the screen.
body: The 3 to 5 key functions are still the right ones.
Each function is rated red, yellow or green.

slides.title: Can you count each widget every week?
slides.headline: Can you count each widget every week?
notes: Confirm each output widget and input widget. If the team does not yet forecast the company widget week over week, start now.
slides.support: Work from the end of the flow back to the start.
body: Every hand-off has a named widget.
Each widget is countable. It is not revenue or cash.
Its owner controls it and counts it every week.

slides.title: Does each critical number tell you the function is working?
slides.headline: Does each critical number tell you the function is working?
notes: Focus on a few critical numbers, at most four, on the KFFM.
slides.support: Look at the number beside each function.
body: The number moves when the work gets better or worse.
Its owner looks at it every day.

slides.title: What are your real days to cash?
slides.headline: What are your real days to cash?
notes: Compare with the days the team estimated last time.
slides.support: Add the days each function really took last quarter.
body: Which function added the most days?

slides.title: Has a good X emerged?
slides.headline: Has a good X emerged?
notes: Profit per X is optional before the annual. If no good X has emerged, leave it blank.
slides.support: Name Profit per X only if a good X has emerged.
body: X is usually a widget from the KFFM.
In the example, X is a subscription: $300 profit per subscription a year.

terms.tip: Jim Collins’s economic engine, from Good to Great. It is the one profit ratio that, raised steadily over time, does the most to drive your economics. Here, profit per subscription: profit divided by the average number of active subscriptions. Allison owns hitting the target, $300 a year.

slides.title: Go through all six levers on your KFFM.
slides.headline: Go through all six levers on your KFFM.
notes: Go lever by lever: quantity, conversion, price, timing, capacity, cost. For each one, ask its owner what they did to push it last quarter and what moved.
A lever nobody is pushing is a finding. Write it down.
Then the team picks the lever that moves cash fastest this quarter. Name the function, the widget and the owner.
Take the chosen lever into the QHAG as a priority candidate.
slides.support: Put your KFFM on the screen. Take one lever at a time.
body: Are you pushing it? What moved last quarter?
Then: which lever moves cash fastest this quarter?
Name the function, the widget and the owner.
